clue.text: Spitting feathers? Maybe just depressed

definitions.meaning: read literally, a creature spitting out feathers has down, soft plumage, held between its lips

explanation.surface: Someone furious, spitting feathers, may really just be feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spitting feathers' is a British idiom for being very angry or very thirsty, which steers away from the literal picture of feathers in someone's mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for looking glum and dejected; read literally, it also pictures feathery down held between the lips.

clue.text: Exercises incorporated into speech surgery

indicators.note: one piece is taken into the body of another, so the exercises go inside the speech

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Some exercises built into speech therapy or surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgical procedure is an operation, so surgery here means a medical procedure on the body.

clue.text: Enquired about scent on daughter

parts.note: a wine's nose is its smell or bouquet

explanation.surface: Someone asked questions about a perfume that their daughter was wearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To nose about or nose into is an idiom for prying or asking questions.

clue.text: Professionally, one angles for it

parts.note: a commercial fisherman literally earns from a mesh full of fish, while any business angles for earnings after costs

explanation.definitionFit: Earnings left once all costs are paid off, the goal any business angles for.

clue.text: Champion new flyer

parts.note: a champion of a cause is a hero

explanation.surface: A winner turns out to be a new pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged wading bird, which as a bird is a flyer.

clue.text: Break up in claim of the local authority

indicators.note: breaking the words apart and reassembling them signals a rearrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Someone's demand to split up the town council.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' acts on UP IN CLAIM, whose nine letters rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describing a town or city council and its local government.

clue.text: Vessel regularly having turbo on auto

indicators.note: taking letters at even intervals, every second one, through the words turbo on auto

explanation.surface: A boat with its turbo engine set to automatic.
explanation.definitionFit: A German submarine of the world wars, a type of naval vessel.

clue.text: She entertains vacant sycophant wearing new shoes

indicators.note: the sycophant has the shoes on, so those letters wrap around the sycophant's letters
made new, the letters of shoes are put into a fresh order
emptied of its inner letters, only the first and last letters of sycophant remain

explanation.surface: A flatterer in new shoes at a party she is throwing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the shoes and 'vacant' empties the sycophant; 'wearing' pictures the flatterer in the shoes, so the shoe letters wrap round the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who receives and looks after guests at a party or event.

clue.text: Prevent letters in Times covering the West of Yorkshire

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit around and cover the other piece
the letters in the word Times are taken and reordered
in an across-style reading the west, left-hand end, of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor tries to stop letters to The Times about West Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters in' reworks TIMES into STMIE, and 'covering' places it round Y, the westernmost letter of Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To block or hinder someone, originally a golfing term for a ball obstructing the line to the hole.

clue.text: Hair loss of leader from pressure

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, which is dropped

parts.note: stress is pressure or strain

explanation.surface: Losing hair through stress at work, as a team leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a lock or long strand of hair.

clue.text: Turn, say, on overthrown dictator so described

indicators.note: overturned and thrown into disorder, the letters of the three words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A political speech urging people to turn on a toppled dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overthrown' works on all three words, TURN SAY ON, together.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruel and oppressive, the adjective one would apply to a despot.

clue.text: Density found in tighter weave

indicators.note: one letter is placed inside the other word

parts.note: tighter with money means stingier, meaner
D is the symbol for density in physics

explanation.surface: A tighter weave produces denser fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind or wander in a twisting course, as a river does.

clue.text: Cause of getting hot under the collar?

definitions.text: Cause of getting hot under the collar?

parts.words: Cause of getting hot under the collar?
parts.note: the idiom means getting angry, but literally it is something worn under a shirt collar that might make one warm

explanation.definitionFit: A strip of cloth knotted round the neck and worn under a shirt collar.

clue.text: Looking to start early, yet ill natured generally

indicators.note: the start of each of the following words is taken, one letter per word

explanation.surface: Keen to get going early, yet generally a grumpy sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Watching or regarding closely, the present participle of the verb to look at.

clue.text: The Roman captured by trained regular fighter

indicators.note: one piece is held inside the other
trained into a new shape, the letters of regular are rearranged

parts.note: il is the Italian word for the, as a modern Roman would say it

explanation.surface: A Roman taken prisoner by a well-drilled professional soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Roman' uses the Italian word for 'the'; 'trained' marks the anagram of regular, and 'captured by' puts the Italian article inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a small irregular force fighting against regular troops.

clue.text: Confront mobs in masks

parts.note: to confront is to face
packs are gangs or mobs

explanation.surface: Standing up to rioting crowds whose faces are hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Beauty treatments spread over the skin like a mask, a cosmetic sense of the clue word.

clue.text: Trappings for prisoner crossing a capital

indicators.note: the prisoner stretches across, around, the other pieces

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
Paris is the capital of France

explanation.surface: A convict being moved across a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamental coverings for a horse, hence fine clothing or trappings.

clue.text: Castro worried with CIA involvement in the country

indicators.note: worried as a dog worries a bone, the letters of the words are shaken up

explanation.surface: Fidel Castro is fretting over American spies meddling in his nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' acts on CASTRO together with CIA; 'with ... involvement' says the agency's letters join the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A Central American republic, a nation lying between Nicaragua and Panama.

clue.text: A handy projection?

parts.note: handy suggests convenient, but read as relating to the hand it describes something sticking out at the end of a digit

explanation.definitionFit: The extreme end of a digit, literally a projection of the hand.

clue.text: Bush, if such a change is possible

indicators.note: the words may be changed around, so their letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A remark about whether a politician named Bush might ever change.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering shrub with drooping purple and red blooms, an ornamental bush.

clue.text: Says thing is to sing

parts.note: someone with this speech defect pronounces an s sound as th, so the word sing comes out as thing

explanation.definitionFit: Speaks with a speech impediment that turns s sounds into th.

clue.text: Short description of safety first on sailing vessel

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word safety is taken

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A brief outline of safety procedures on board a yacht.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief outline or summary account, such as a character study.

clue.text: King, pinned by castle and queen, is more obvious

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'King, pinned by castle and queen, is more obvious': LEAR inside C...ER needs C, but 'castle' gives no C (no standard abbreviation); likely OCR or transcription fault, and no source found.
annotationWithheld.clue: King, pinned by castle and queen, is more obvious

clue.text: Half of them are sick of such correspondence

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word them, here its second pair of letters

parts.note: to ail is to be ill

explanation.surface: Half the people who get these messages are fed up with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic messages, the modern form of letter writing.

clue.text: Soldiers manage another race

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: Army men organise a second contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeat of a contest, run again after a dispute or false start.

clue.text: One's heart a prisoner to it

definitions.text: One's heart a prisoner to it

parts.words: One's heart a prisoner to it
parts.note: sounds like romantic captivity, but literally describes the bony enclosure that shuts the heart inside the chest

explanation.definitionFit: The bony frame of the chest, which encloses the heart and lungs.

clue.text: Entices cricketers to accept one

indicators.note: one piece takes the other in

parts.note: bats are batsmen in cricket
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A team lures cricketers by offering them a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Lures or tempts, as with food on a hook.

clue.text: Sunday shopping area with branches offering offensive items

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre
arms are branches, as of a river or organisation

explanation.surface: A Sunday trip to a shopping centre with branches selling distasteful goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Firearms such as pistols and rifles, weapons for offence.

clue.text: I left one with a chart, initially of the lower intestine

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the initial letter of chart is taken

explanation.surface: A patient says they left with a chart of their lower bowel.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the ileum, the lowest part of the small intestine, in an older spelling.

clue.text: A sucker for listener's sharp rebuke

parts.note: a flea is a blood-sucking insect
a listener hears with their ear, so this is the place for it: in their ear

explanation.surface: A lollipop for someone listening to a stern telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a scolding that sends someone away chastened.
